Container.Name: YA-WAMF
Container.Overview: YA-WAMF (Yet Another WhosAtMyFeeder) identifies birds at your feeder from Frigate NVR events using local machine-learning models. It shows a real-time dashboard, correlates visual detections with BirdNET-Go audio, enriches species with taxonomy, and can send notifications. This is the monolithic image (web UI and backend in one container). It needs a running Frigate instance publishing events over MQTT; point it at your Frigate URL below. See the Unraid setup guide for the full walkthrough.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: bird birds feeder frigate birdnet classification nvr
Container.Description: YA-WAMF identifies birds at your feeder from Frigate NVR events using local ML models, with a real-time dashboard, optional BirdNET-Go audio correlation, taxonomy enrichment, and notifications. Requirements: a reachable Frigate instance and MQTT broker. Configuration is stored in /config and the detections database and media cache live in /data. Optional Intel GPU or NPU acceleration can be enabled by passing the matching device (see the hardware-acceleration guide).

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the YA-WAMF web interface (container listens on 8080).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Detections database (SQLite) and cached media. Can grow with retention; keep on fast storage.

Config.Name: Frigate URL
Config.Description: Base URL of your Frigate instance (for the MQTT-driven event pipeline and media fetch).

Config.Name: Timezone (TZ)
Config.Description: Container timezone, e.g. Europe/London. Leave blank for UTC.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the container runs as (Unraid default 'nobody' is 99).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the container runs as (Unraid default 'users' is 100).
